The rule reads a column used by MAX or VALUES in a measure as a fact column. Release Sequence is the ordering attribute of the Release dimension (Outturn as at Release takes its maximum, and Release sorts by it) and a reader may want it visible.

The rule matches columns by name and finds the Financial Year of Fiscal Year, which is the one side of the relationship and the only year a report author should pick; the foreign key with the same name is in Fiscal Period.
The flag is on every row of the phased plan on purpose, so that the derived label travels with the data; Scenario carries the same flag for the scenario.
Fiscal Period relates to Fiscal Year because the plan is published by year and outturn by period; one year dimension filters both facts (docs/model.md, what was awkward in the star schema, item 2).
Account relates to Statement Line, so that a statement line filters the accounts it adds up and, through them, the outturn; the layout is authored once and not copied onto the account.
The grain code (A to D) is the key of Plan Grain and also the label that people read next to the grain name.
